title: Meklit Wants to Fill the Eight-Hour Silence in Ethiopia's Daycares
desc:
For many parents in Addis Ababa, the moment a child enters daycare, the day largely disappears.
At 4pm, they may get a sentence: “She ate. She’s fine.”
The problem is not necessarily poor care. It is that there is often no system for recording what happens between drop-off and pickup. Meals, naps, injuries, health changes and developmental observations can disappear with the caregiver’s memory.
Meklit, an Ethiopian childcare platform, is trying to build that missing layer of infrastructure. Its fifth product iteration combines daily care logs, play-based learning, health monitoring and parent communication,

title: Industrial production stable in the euro area and up by 0.2% in the EU
desc: Overview In June 2026, compared with May 2026, seasonally adjusted industrial production remained stable in the euro area and increased by 0.2% in the EU, according to first estimates from Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union. In May 2026, industrial production grew by 0.3% in both the euro area and the EU. In June 2026, compared with June 2025, industrial production increased by 0.1% in the euro area and by 0.6% in the EU. Monthly comparison by main industrial grouping and by Member State In the euro area in June 2026, compared with May 2026, industrial production decreased for intermediate goods by 0.8%, increased for energy by 1.5%, decreased for capital goods by 1.4%, increased for durable consumer goods by 0.3%, increased for non-durable consumer goods by 3.0%. In the EU, industrial production decreased for intermediate goods by 0.7%, increased for energy by 1.0%, decreased for capital goods by 0.9%, increased for durable consumer goods by 0.9%, increased for non-durable consumer goods by 2.5%. Among the Member States for which data are available, the highest monthly increases were recorded in Denmark (+5.4%), Croatia (+5.2%), Lithuania and Finland (both +2.1%). The largest decreases were observed in Luxembourg (-10.7%), Portugal (-3.9%) and Estonia (-2.2%). Annual comparison by main industrial grouping and by Member State In the euro area in June 2026, compared with June 2025, industrial production increased for intermediate goods by 0.4%, increased for energy by 0.9%, increased for capital goods by 0.1%, decreased for durable consumer goods by 2.5%, decreased for non-durable consumer goods by 0.5%. In the EU, industrial production increased for intermediate goods by 1.0%, increased for energy by 0.3%, increased for capital goods by 0.9%, decreased for durable consumer goods by 0.9%, decreased for non-durable consumer goods by 0.3%. Among the Member States for which data are available, the highest annual increases were recorded in Lithuania (+7.7%), Denmark (+6.1%) and Poland (+4.9%). The largest decreases were observed in Luxembourg (-7.9%), Romania (-5.6%) and Estonia (-4.6%). The annual percentage change has been revised from -1.2% to -0.1% in the euro area and from -0.3% to +0.6% in the EU . Methods and definitions The index of industrial production measures the evolution of the volume of production for industry excluding construction, based on data adjusted for calendar and seasonal effects. Seasonally adjusted euro area and EU series are calculated by aggregating the seasonally adjusted national data. Total industry covers NACE Rev. 2 sections B to D. Missing observations from Member States for recent months are estimated for the calculation of the euro area and the EU aggregates. Geographical information The Euro area (EA21) includes Belgium, Bulgaria, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Slovenia, Slovakia and Finland. The European Union (EU27) includes Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Hungary, Malta, the Netherlands, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Finland and Sweden.
